newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian lending rate up to 11.6 pct from 10.3.
newsitem.headline: Croatian lending rate up to 11.6 pct from 10.3.

text.p: Croatia's average lending rate rose to 11.6 percent on Tuesday from 10.3, boosted by a larger volume of term loans granted at higher rates, dealers said..
They put the daily settlements at 19.6 million kuna, which left a surplus of 30.4 million kuna on the supply side.
Of the 12 million kuna fresh borrowings, about a half were granted at a steady call money rate of 10.5 percent.
But "rates for interbank term loans, varying between 13, 15 and 16 percent, raised the weighted lending rate," a dealer said.
Insurers rolled over previous 7.6 million kuna loans at steady nine and 14 percent.
The central bank calculated its kuna midrates for Wednesday weaker at 6.0420 against the dollar and firmer 3.5726 against the German mark. -- Zoran Radosavljevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
